slides.headline: What does it mean?
slides.body: GST and other tax obligations fall on fixed dates, regardless of how your cash flow is tracking that quarter. Because the amounts can be substantial relative to day-to-day cash, many businesses find tax time is when cash-flow pressure shows up most clearly.

slides.headline: Why it matters
bullet_points: BAS and tax dates are fixed, cash flow isn't
Quarterly obligations can be sizeable relative to daily cash
Growth can increase GST liability faster than expected
Falling behind can lead to ATO debt and added pressure

caption:
Because BAS and tax obligations land on fixed dates no matter how trading is going, they're one of the most predictable, and most commonly underestimated, sources of cash-flow pressure. GST collected during the quarter can feel like revenue if it isn't set aside deliberately.

If you do fall behind, specialist finance exists specifically to address ATO debt, rather than treating it the same as any other cash shortfall.
